chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Is there no free man who can leave this chewed morsel to those who like it? Certainly, the only price for yourselves is Paradise. Therefore, do not sell yourself except for Paradise.

key_terms.اللُّمَاظَة: A chewed morsel; a metaphor for the world being partially consumed or less desirable.
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise; the ultimate reward and the only true price for the soul.
key_terms.حُرٌّ: A free man; one who is not enslaved by worldly desires.

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali mean by calling the world a 'chewed morsel'?
ai.summary: In this famous saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of a 'chewed morsel' (lumaẓah) to illustrate the world's transient and consumed nature, urging believers to view their souls as precious commodities to be sold exclusively for Paradise. This concept of 'selling the self' (bay' al-nafs) is central to Shia asceticism, emphasizing that worldly life is merely a temporary market where the ultimate transaction is the exchange of one's eternal soul for divine reward.
